safety_verdicts.content: Patient is currently sexually active with a regular partner, with the last unprotected intercourse occurring 4 days ago.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated notes sexually active with same partner but does not include last unprotected intercourse 4 days ago.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the timing of last unprotected intercourse can reduce salience of pregnancy- or STI-related differentials (e.g., early pregnancy/ectopic, PID) when evaluating lower abdominal pain. Although contraception is in place and pregnancy testing was discussed, this missing detail could still delay appropriate escalation or targeted testing.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient denies any chest pain, shortness of breath, palpitations, headaches, or visual symptoms.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated denies SOB/palpitations/headache/visual disturbance but does not mention absence of chest pain.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to document absence of chest pain is unlikely to affect management in a presentation centered on lower abdominal pain with urinary symptoms. This is primarily a minor completeness issue in review-of-systems documentation.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient to have a review in 24-48 hours if symptoms are not improving.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated advises return if no improvement 'in a few days' but does not specify review in 24–48 hours.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Replacing a specific 24–48 hour review window with a vaguer “few days” can delay reassessment if symptoms persist or worsen, which is important when the differential includes potentially time-sensitive conditions (e.g., evolving UTI/pyelonephritis, appendicitis, pregnancy-related causes). This could lead to delayed diagnosis and treatment escalation.
